records.limitations: Single-center cohort acquired in the Brigham and Women's Hospital AMIGO suite; non-glioma lesions represent a minority (11 metastases, 11 other lesions), and longitudinal post-discharge follow-up MRI is not included.

records.limitations: Small single-center cohort (23 patients, St. Olavs University Hospital) restricted to low-grade gliomas without modern WHO 2021 molecular markers (IDH/1p19q), limiting generalizability across ultrasound vendors and high-grade tumors.

records.highlights: The canonical multi-institutional adult diffuse glioma mpMRI benchmark (T1, T1ce, T2, T2-FLAIR) co-registered to SRI24 1 mm isotropic space with neuroradiologist-refined enhancing tumor, necrotic core, and peritumoral edema masks plus MGMT radiogenomics labels.
records.limitations: Pre-processed skull-stripped preoperative scans only; masks rely on harmonized clinical routine acquisitions primarily from North American and European centers without raw DICOM headers or post-treatment timepoints.

records.highlights: First large-scale multi-institutional BraTS benchmark dedicated exclusively to post-surgical and post-treatment diffuse gliomas across 7 academic centers, introducing explicit resection cavity (RC) labels alongside enhancing tissue, non-enhancing core, and FLAIR hyperintensity.
records.limitations: Distinguishing true residual/recurrent tumor from post-surgical blood products and treatment-related radiation changes remains inherently challenging; linked clinical treatment dates and genomic markers are not bundled in the challenge split.

records.limitations: Only a subset of the 1,303 curated studies (402 training studies) is released publicly with labels; tiny sub-5 mm metastases suffer high inter-rater variability and primary systemic cancer histologies are not uniformly provided.

records.highlights: Landmark global-equity neuroimaging cohort of 146 patients retrospectively curated across clinical diagnostic centers in Nigeria, enabling rigorous stress-testing of domain adaptation and low-field / heterogeneous clinical MRI generalization outside the Global North.
records.limitations: Modest cohort size sourced exclusively from Nigerian clinical centers; lower magnetic field strengths (including 1.5T and routine anisotropic protocols) and advanced late-stage tumor presentations create substantial domain shift without paired molecular genomics.

records.limitations: Training distribution remains heavily skewed toward adult diffuse glioma relative to rare or pediatric subtypes; relies on standardized BraTS skull-stripped 4-sequence mpMRI and lacks longitudinal or intraoperative scans.

records.highlights: First BraTS computational pathology benchmark co-developed with RANO-Pathology and AI-RANO working groups, offering 309,118 neuropathologist-annotated FFPE H&E glioblastoma patches across 11 institutions covering cellular tumor, necrosis, microvascular proliferation, and infiltration.
records.limitations: Patch-level ex-vivo FFPE H&E representation lacks spatial whole-slide context and paired preoperative MRI or molecular genomic readouts; stain and scanner variability across the 11 sites can impact out-of-domain robustness.

records.highlights: Uniformly acquired 3T preoperative MRI dataset of 501 WHO grade II-IV diffuse gliomas pairing 3D structural sequences with HARDI diffusion (DTI) and 3D arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion, expert tumor masks, survival outcomes, and IDH/MGMT/1p19q molecular labels.
records.limitations: Single-center, single-vendor 3T GE scanner protocol limits direct assessment of cross-vendor scanner shift; preoperative baseline scans only without post-resection or longitudinal recurrence follow-up.

records.limitations: Single-health-system US cohort; manual neuroradiologist mask corrections and digitized H&E whole-slide images exist only for a subset of cases (remaining masks are automated ensembles), and molecular marker completeness (e.g., MGMT, targeted genomic panels) varies across patients.

records.limitations: Single-center retrospective US cohort (University of Missouri); initial segmentation contours were generated via nnU-Net before expert refinement, and follow-up interval cadence reflects heterogeneous routine clinical care.

records.limitations: Small single-center Spanish cohort (40 patients) restricted to patients who achieved gross-total or near-total resection and subsequently experienced documented recurrence, introducing selection bias against biopsy-only cases.

records.limitations: Single-center Swiss cohort (Bern University Hospital); provided voxel-wise segmentations are automated outputs (DeepBraTumIA and HD-GLIO-AUTO) rather than manually corrected gold standards, and molecular status is missing for a subset of patients.

records.highlights: Unique neuro-oncology radiotherapy and longitudinal progression cohort of 180 primary GBM patients combining planning CT, 4-sequence MRI, full DICOM RTSTRUCT/RTPLAN/RTDOSE radiotherapy objects, 1-8 longitudinal follow-up scans, IDH/MGMT markers, and progression vs. pseudoprogression labels.
records.limitations: Controlled DUA required via TCIA Restricted License because non-defaced structural head scans carry facial-reconstruction re-identification risk; single-center Russian cohort with variable follow-up counts and partial molecular completeness.

records.limitations: Single-center UK cohort (National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London) with 25 procedures under a non-commercial, no-derivatives license (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); annotations capture temporal presence rather than pixel-level instrument segmentation masks.

records.limitations: Derived from the same single-center London surgical cohort of 25 videos as PitVis; template-structured frame-level QA pairs may exhibit linguistic homogeneity and non-commercial licensing (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) restricts commercial deployment.

records.limitations: Requires registration via institutional portal and non-commercial CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms; acquired exclusively on NIO Laser Imaging Systems with patch-level weak patient labels for most slides and no paired preoperative MRI.

python -c "import glob, nibabel as nib; imgs = glob.glob('./data/atlas-v2/**/*T1w.nii.gz', recursive=True); print(f'Loaded {len(imgs)} T1w volumes')"
records.highlights: Largest multi-site manually segmented chronic and subacute stroke lesion MRI dataset (1,271 T1w scans across 44 international ENIGMA cohorts: 33 train/test + 11 hidden generalizability cohorts), widely adopted alongside BraTS for neuro-foundation model pretraining, lesion-resilient brain parcellation, and cross-pathology generalization.
records.limitations: Single-modality T1-weighted MRI only (lacking acute DWI/ADC or FLAIR sequences); access requires an institutional USC/INDI Data Use Agreement prohibiting redistribution, and acute ischemic/hemorrhagic strokes are underrepresented.
